title: Tenant-fenced rollout safeguard and fastpatch playbook for canary regressions
creator: Evelyn Carter
description: Context: Recent model rollouts across Hosted and Dedicated clusters surfaced a regression affecting a small but high-value set of tenants in Private deployments. This ticket captures an operational playbook to (1) rapidly fence affected tenants, (2) coordinate cross-environment rollback or fastpatch, and (3) provide consistent customer communication and post-mortem artifacts. Goals: minimize blast radius, keep unaffected tenants online, provide a single source-of-truth for escalation and triage, and codify actions that SRE/Oncall, infra, and PMs can take during a canary-quality regression.
runbook_steps: Detect & tag: Oncall triages alerts and verifies signal. Tag incident with 'canary-regression' and list suspected model version and deployment targets (hosted/dedicated/private).

Tenant fencing: If regression is tenant-specific, use tenant-slice routing to quarantine affected tenants to read-only or to a stable model variant. Preference: soft-fence (traffic mirroring to fallback) before hard-fence (complete traffic cut).

Traffic split & fallback: Move 100% of traffic from canary variant to the currently-known-good model variant in the same environment. If unavailable, reroute to nearest compatible region or Dedicated pool. Ensure KV cache compatibility or invalidate small prefix slices as needed.

Cross-env coordination: Notify Dedicated and Private deployment owners. Use the 'crossenv-roll' Slack channel with cc to oncall-sre, infra-leads, PM, and customer success. Explicitly list tenants affected and their emergency contact.

Patch vs rollback decision: Decision tree: (a) If root cause is model artifact (promoted weights), prefer rollback; (b) If inference code bug limited to runtime branch, prefer hotpatch (fastpatch) with canary tests; (c) If ambiguous, roll back to last-promoted commit and start safe fastpatch branch.

Apply remediation: Execute rollback or deploy hotpatch to canary then ramp to remaining pods using staged rollout (10%, 50%, 100%). Monitor token-level quality metrics (BLEU-like / embedding-sim similarity / key prompts) and latency and error rates.
Data & cache reconciliation: For rollbacks that change tokenization/kvcache semantics, coordinate cache flushes on affected nodes and notify customers if session-level continuity is impacted.
Customer comms: Draft a template status update with timeline, impact, and mitigation steps. Customer Success to send targeted messages to high-value tenants within 60 minutes of actioned remediation.
Post-incident: Create postmortem, link PRs and dashboards, add regression tests to the rollout gate, and schedule a follow-up retro within 7 days.
acceptance_criteria: A documented and rehearsed tenant-fencing flow exists usable by oncall within 15 minutes
Rollback or hotpatch actions are automated and validated in CI/CD for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment paths
Customer communications template and contacts list are available in the incident runbook
Two new automated canary checks (semantic quality and prompt-sensitivity) are added to the rollout pipeline
